basis: Defining neurodevelopmental impairment, seizures and abnormal tone; constipation alone does not establish intestinal damage.
Presynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder; persistent ptosis 80-99%, ophthalmoplegia 30-79%; muscle atrophy and arthrogryposis 30-79%. Respiratory weakness is neuromuscular.
Mild inherited photodermatosis; no evidence that damaging ocular or neurologic manifestations commonly occur in this specific subtype.
Isolated familial dilated cardiomyopathy with ventricular systolic dysfunction.
Urea cycle defect causes ammonia neurotoxicity: seizures 3/3 and coma 2/3 reported patients. Reduced hepatic enzyme activity alone does not establish liver injury.
Congenital antibody deficiency with B-cell deficiency; recurrent infections do not establish common direct damage to another organ.
Chronic endometritis commonly reflects persistent endometrial infection; the reproductive organ itself has no axis.
Lysosomal storage disorder; intellectual disability, scoliosis and gingival overgrowth each occur in 80-99%. Additional dental and skeletal abnormalities occur in 30-79%.
Immune-mediated airway disease with severe obstruction and respiratory failure; altered consciousness does not establish separate neurologic damage.
Defined by pathogenic inflammatory injury of the intestinal mucosa, including infectious forms such as dysentery.
Congenital heart defects, craniosynostosis and absent teeth define the syndrome; ptosis is also a defining diagnostic feature.
Neonatal Candida infection; the concept does not specify a site or establish common damage to any particular organ.
Carcinoma explicitly arises in perianal skin; intestinal origin or common intestinal invasion is not established.
Organic acid disorder defined by leukoencephalopathy, developmental impairment and ataxia. The discordant infectious encephalitis annotation does not establish an infectious mechanism.
Benign tumour of the uterine cervix; reproductive tissue has no axis.
Primary penile carcinoma; reproductive organs have no axis, and no other qualifying organ involvement is established.
Defining cerebellar malformation, trigeminal dysfunction and scalp alopecia; corneal opacity occurs in 80-99%, strabismus in 31/39 and visual impairment in 30-79%.
Hereditary axonal neuropathy; progressive distal muscle atrophy and fixed foot deformities are characteristic and common (>30%).
Definition and anatomical location identify a vulvar vestibular gland tumour; urinary ancestry does not establish urethral origin.
Pancreatic adenoma with digestive-system neoplasm ancestry; endocrine origin or hormone dysfunction is not specified.
Acquired skeletal myopathy with muscle atrophy and myosin loss; critical illness and treatments are triggers, not additional affected organs.
Skeletal dysplasia with slender bones, vertebral abnormalities and joint laxity; hypospadias is a structural urethral anomaly reported in 10/11 patients.
Marrow failure; intellectual disability 31%, microphthalmia 61% and thumb malformations >=31%. Pigment changes lack demonstrated tissue injury; renal anomalies individually <30%.
Skin blistering and muscular dystrophy define disease; persistent ophthalmoplegia 80-99% and dental enamel defects 30-79%. Language annotations are discordant with the syndrome.
Central disorder of sleep-wake regulation with persistent hypersomnolence; a neurologic sleep disorder despite psychiatric-style coding.
